capabilities: Sync selected vault subfolders with GitHub repos
Auto-commit and push after edits and auto-pull on an interval
Resolve merge conflicts in a side-by-side modal
Sign in with GitHub via OAuth device flow
Map each shared folder to its own repo
extras: Setup requires manually copying main.js, manifest.json, and styles.css into the plugins folder. A planned MCP server would let Claude act as a collaborator; sync logic is designed to be reusable outside Obsidian.
intentEvidence: Why not Obsidian Git? Obsidian Git tracks your entire vault as one repo.
motivation: The author wanted collaboration without third-party servers, subscriptions, or manual git work, keeping notes under the user's own GitHub ownership.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in collaboration, and syncing a whole vault through git forces collaborators to share everything and manage commits manually.

relations.evidence: Why not Obsidian Git? Obsidian Git tracks your entire vault as one repo.

summary: GitHub-based collaboration plugin that syncs individual vault subfolders with automatic push/pull and a side-by-side conflict resolution modal.
